description: F-CORE-028: the chart of accounts as a screen can afford to read it — number, name, type, subtype, status, and nothing else. Both facts an application needs most were published only where it could not use them. `subtype` says what an account IS FOR — which one is the bank, which the cash box, which receivables and payables — and it lived in `journalExport.data.accounts`, behind five streams with a SHA-256 each; `datevExport(kind: accounts)` is cheap but gives number, name and type, because it is DATEV-shaped master data by definition. So an application preselecting the receivable account for a payment had to read the PACK it was created from, which is the chart the tenant started with rather than the chart it has: one `createAccount` and the guess is wrong. `status` is the read side of `lockAccount` — the operation existed and no affordable projection said whether it had been used, so a screen could lock an account and not show that it was locked, and the only honest test was to post into it and read the refusal. Deliberately small: no balances (trialBalance), no movements (accountSheet), no hashes. Ordered by account number over Unicode code points.

expect.comment: An account the pack did not bring. It is the case that makes reading the pack instead of the chart wrong.

Every account, in account-number order, with its role and its status. The locked 8400 is still in the list — a locked account is part of the chart, it just refuses postings, and a list that hid it would make the lock invisible again.
